report:
I have strong, converging evidence. Here's my synthesis.

## Conclusion

The claim is **well supported by evidence**, not false. Multiple randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, and international guidelines confirm that starting tenofovir (usually tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) in the third trimester (around 28–32 weeks) in pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B and high viral load (typically HBV DNA ≥200,000 IU/mL) significantly reduces mother-to-child transmission (MTCT), on top of standard infant immunoprophylaxis (HBIG + vaccine).

**Evidence supporting this:**
- A large meta-analysis in *Hepatology* concluded that "antiviral therapy improves HBV suppression and reduces MTCT in women with chronic HBV infection with high viral load compared to the use of hepatitis B immunoglobulin and vaccination alone," with tenofovir, lamivudine, and telbivudine all shown safe in pregnancy (https://journals.lww.com/hep/fulltext/10.1002/hep.28302~antiviral-therapy-in-chronic-hepatitis-b-viral-infection).
- A systematic review/meta-analysis in *Lancet Infectious Diseases*, conducted specifically to inform the 2020 WHO guidelines, evaluated efficacy and safety of peripartum antiviral prophylaxis and found benefit for high-risk mothers (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/laninf/article/PIIS1473-3099(20)30586-7/abstract).
- WHO's official guidance states plainly: "WHO recommends that pregnant women testing positive for HBV infection (HBsAg positive) with an HBV DNA ≥5.3 log10 IU/mL (≥200,000 IU/mL) receive tenofovir prophylaxis from the 28th week of pregnancy until at least birth to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HBV" (https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/05e2abad-5fa6-4479-b583-1eb5bbc27315/content).
- A supporting narrative review corroborates that emerging trial data show third-trimester antiviral therapy prevents immunoprophylaxis failure in high-viral-load mothers (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7136311/).

This is a strong, consistent scientific and clinical consensus—not a fringe or disproven claim.
